exposure: Receipt of prenatal care in the first trimester
cohort: A representative sample of Rhode Island women who recently gave birth, categorized by the presence or absence of disabilities.
finding: Women with disabilities in Rhode Island reported significant disparities in health care utilization, health behaviors, and health status, and were more likely to experience stressful life events, medical complications during pregnancy, receive less first-trimester prenatal care, and have preterm births and low-birth-weight babies compared to nondisabled women.
mod_finding: There was no difference in the rates of cesarean section between women with and without disabilities.
